title: TransportEnvelope
description: The eight WebSocket frame shapes exchanged between the laptop (server) and the phone (client); see docs/camera-sync-design.md Sec 4.2 and Sec 4.4, docs/steps/step-20-brief.md (query/answer), docs/shepherd-steering-plan.md step 21 (steer) and contracts/README.md 'Transport envelope'. The reserved type 'location' (phone -> laptop, defined in a later step) and any other unrecognised 'type' are valid JSON that a receiver logs and ignores -- they are deliberately out of scope for this schema, which only documents the shapes the laptop and phone actually exchange today.

t1.description: Laptop send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.
Echoed laptop send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

t2.description: Phone receive time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

t3.description: Phone send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

health.description: Phone -> laptop. One report of the feedback manager's stale-drop ring (10 one-second buckets of {received, staleDropped}); a rising rate is the trigger for the docs/camera-sync-design.md Sec 3.4 automatic fallback. Advisory only: the laptop's health monitor still steps rungs and flips to the local detector without it, and a report older than 3 s (after clock conversion) is ignored, so a dead signal can never drive a switch.

t_phone_ms.description: When the phone produced this report, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds in the PHONE clock (the laptop converts before judging freshness).

window_ms.description: Width of the whole ring in milliseconds (10 one-second buckets = 10000).

received.description: Events the feedback manager received inside the window.

stale_dropped.description: Of those, the ones dropped for arriving past their TTL (Sec 4.4).

stale_drop_rate.description: stale_dropped / received over the complete buckets; 0 when received is 0. At or above 0.2 over at least 2 complete buckets the laptop flips to the local detector.

complete_buckets.description: How many of the ring's one-second buckets are fully elapsed. Fewer than 2 makes the rate meaningless, and the laptop ignores the report.

phone_frame.description: One rectilinear JPEG from the phone's front camera, captured when the query was asked. Mirroring is off, so image-left is the wearer's left.

jpeg_b64.description: Standard base64 of the JPEG bytes (<= ~2 MB decoded).

hfov_deg.description: Horizontal field of view of the image as sent, degrees.

query.description: Phone -> laptop. A spoken question about the surroundings ('Hey Cane, is there a bathroom around?'). The laptop answers with exactly one 'answer' frame carrying the same query_id; a newer query supersedes an older one still in flight.

kind.description: find: look for 'target' all around. describe_around: summarise the 360 view. describe_front: describe the phone frame (X4 crops optional).

target.description: What to find ('bathroom'); required for kind 'find', null otherwise.

utterance.description: The recognised words after the wake word, verbatim.

t_phone_ms.description: When the phone sent the query, PHONE-clock Unix-epoch ms.

answer.description: Laptop -> phone. The one reply to a 'query'. The phone turns bearing_deg into its own direction words; subject and detail are short noun phrases, never directions.

subject.description: What was found ('restroom sign'). Required when status is 'found'.

bearing_deg.description: Torso-relative, same convention as AwarenessEvent.bearing_deg (0 ahead, negative left). Only with status 'found'.

detail.description: Extra context ('past the elevators'), or the whole description when status is 'described'.

latency_ms.description: Laptop-side time from receiving the query to sending this answer.

diag.description: Phone -> laptop. One line of the phone's black-box recorder (what the mic heard, wake-word and intent decisions, what was spoken, link changes, mic level). Advisory and write-only: the laptop appends it to logs/phone-YYYYMMDD.jsonl. Text and numbers only, never audio.

data.text: hey cane is there a bathroom

steer.description: Laptop -> phone. One continuous steering command per sensing tick -- Shepherd's stage 7 over our existing WebSocket instead of their 12-byte BLE packet (docs/shepherd-steering-plan.md Sec 0 row 7 and step 21). It says which way the passable gap lies and how hard to lean that way; the phone owns the actuation (integrator, cue, decay). Deliberately perishable: a steer command ages like a car, so ttl_ms is 400 ms and an expired one decays the cue to neutral rather than being held. In local-fallback mode the laptop sends no steer frame at all -- a zero steer would be a silent fake of having looked.

t_capture_ms.description: The capture time of the frame this command was computed from, same PHONE-clock window and semantics as AwarenessEvent.t_capture_ms. Echoed from the cloud, never re-read from a clock, so the phone can age the command against its own clock directly.

ttl_ms.description: Time-to-live in milliseconds, same bounds as AwarenessEvent.ttl_ms. Always 400 (STEER_TTL_MS) today: the most perishable row of the Sec 4.4 staleness table.

steer.description: The steering command, positive = right. sign(gapDirection) * sqrt(abs(gapDirection)) * proximityFactor, clamped to [-1, 1]. 0 means 'no lean', which happens both in a clear corridor (proximity 0) and when blocked.

proximity.description: Shepherd's proximityFactor: 0 clear, 1 at the stopping distance. clamp((d_clear - d_min) / (d_clear - d_stop), 0, 1) with d_stop 0.60 m and d_clear 3.00 m. Read it together with proximity_anchored -- unanchored, it is a band, not a number.

gap_bearing_deg.description: Torso-relative bearing of the chosen gap's centroid, degrees, 0 = ahead, + = right. Same half-open (-180, 180] convention as AwarenessEvent.bearing_deg, including the trap: a producer converting radians to degrees can emit exactly -180.0 and be rejected, and must normalize by adding 360. The forward ring only spans -90..+90, but the bound is the contract's, not the ring's.

blocked.description: True when no contiguous passable run was at least BODY_WIDTH_M (0.70 m) wide -- there is no gap to steer into. gap_bearing_deg is still present (every key always is) and points at the least-bad column.

proximity_anchored.description: Whether the ground-plane scale fit that turns relative depth into metres was accepted (Sec 2.3). False on stairs, a slope, or a floor hidden by a crowd; the phone then treats proximity as a band, the same 'trust the band, not the metre' rule RangeTrust.swift already applies to phone ranges. It is never a reason to ignore the frame.

source.description: Which sensing path produced it. Closed at x4_cloud because depth only runs in the cloud today; a local depth path is a one-line addition here, never a free string on the wire.
